surprising_finding: A flat's own old rent beats everything else, even when it is stale. The typical own rent we used was about 20 months old, yet once indexed it missed by $41 on Fold A, against $100 for a recent suburb, bedrooms and parking median. The second surprise was in the supplied input: its parking and bedrooms track each flat's latest advert, so a simple date split quietly shows a model the answer. We rebuilt those fields as known at each cutoff.
what_worked: Indexing each flat's own last rent to the target date. This took the Fold A anchor bias from -$50 to +$3.62.
Rolling two-month training windows, so each training row faces the same gap as the real task.
Rebuilding parking and bedrooms as known at each cutoff. This removed a hidden leak and created 85 Fold B adverts that test the parking premium directly.
what_didnt: Projecting the rent trend forward. Tuning on Fold B chose to hold the index flat at the cutoff.
Predicting log(rent / anchor) instead of rent. The two were within $0.10 on Fold B, so the choice between them is noise.

The model's own with and without gap. It came out around $17 against a measured $36, because anchors stay fixed between passes. On Fold B the two premiums tied on median error, so we chose the within-building premium for its lower bias on flipped adverts and its higher share within $100.
